intro: 成都武侯祠，位于中华人民共和国四川省成都市武侯区浆洗街街道武侯祠大街231号，是中国唯一的君臣合祀祠庙，由武侯祠、汉昭烈庙及惠陵组成，人们习惯将三者统称为武侯祠。成都武侯祠始建于公元223年修建惠陵（刘备的陵寝）之时，其中武侯祠（诸葛亮的专祠）建于唐以前，初与祭祀刘备（汉昭烈帝）的汉昭烈庙相邻，明朝初年重建时将武侯祠并入，形成了君臣合祀，祠堂与陵园合一的格局。除惠陵以外现存祠庙主体建筑为1672年清康熙年间复建。1984年成立成都武侯祠博物馆，2008年被评为首批国家一级博物馆。

intro_en: Chengdu Wuhou Shrine, located at No. 231 Wuhou Shrine Street, Jinxi Subdistrict, Wuhou District, Chengdu, Sichuan Province, the People's Republic of China, is the only temple in China where an emperor and his minister are worshipped together. It comprises the Wuhou Shrine, the Zhaolie Temple of Han, and Huiling Mausoleum, and people habitually refer to all three collectively as the Wuhou Shrine. Chengdu Wuhou Shrine was first built in 223 AD when Huiling (the tomb of Liu Bei) was constructed; the Wuhou Shrine itself (a shrine dedicated to Zhuge Liang) was built before the Tang Dynasty, initially adjacent to the Zhaolie Temple of Han, which honored Liu Bei (Emperor Zhaolie of Han). During the early Ming Dynasty reconstruction, the Wuhou Shrine was merged into it, forming a layout in which emperor and minister are worshipped together and the shrine and the mausoleum are combined into one. Apart from Huiling, the main existing temple buildings were rebuilt in 1672 during the Kangxi reign of the Qing Dynasty. The Chengdu Wuhou Shrine Museum was established in 1984 and was rated among the first batch of National First-Class Museums in 2008.
